questions.stem: Why is the nucleus considered the control centre of the cell?

options.text: It produces energy in the form of ATP
It controls what substances enter and leave the cell
It contains DNA that regulates cell activities through gene expression
It breaks down worn-out organelles using digestive enzymes

questions.explanation: The nucleus contains the cell's DNA organised into chromosomes, and it controls cell activities by determining which genes are switched on, directing the production of specific proteins.
